raw_response:
I'm 55 this year, and I've been working these 3.8 mu for 30 years. It's just my wife and me now — our son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and sends a bit home, but I don't like asking him for farm money. This land is my responsibility. We're not young anymore, so we hire the rotary tiller and the combine when we have to, but for spraying, irrigation, and moving bags, we do it ourselves. Hiring labor costs at least 150 yuan a day now, and on less than 4 mu there's no margin for that.

For **winter wheat**, I'll plant around October 8th, right after the National Day holiday when the soil is still warm. I use an improved variety — I buy fresh seed every few years from the county supply store, and this year I'm using seed I saved from last year mixed with a little new stock. Before planting, I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu and work it in with the rotary tiller. The extension fellow says I could push 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I've tried that and the extra fertilizer costs don't always come back in yield, especially if spring is dry. I stick with about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu total — the compound gives me some, and then at jointing in late March I topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu if the wheat looks a bit yellow. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings don't freeze, once at jointing when the weather warms up, and once in May during grain filling. The pumping costs add up — electricity isn't cheap — but I've learned the hard way that skipping the spring irrigation is gambling with the crop. I spray herbicide once after emergence, and if I see powdery mildew in April, I might spray fungicide, but only if it looks bad. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu. If the weather holds, I expect about the same.

For **summer maize**, the window is brutal. The wheat comes off around June 12th, and I need to get the maize in within two or three days before the soil dries out. I buy hybrid seed fresh every year — about 50 yuan per mu — because saved seed doesn't breed true. I do one quick pass with the rotary tiller if the stubble is thick, then plant immediately. All the fertilizer goes down at planting: about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu and 10 kg of urea in the furrow. I don't have time to come back and topdress later — the season is too short and we're not as fast as we used to be. I irrigate twice in the summer, usually once in July when it's tasseling and again in August if the rain doesn't come. The summer rains usually help, but you can't count on them. I spray herbicide and insecticide once — the corn borer was bad two years ago and I lost yield, so I don't skip that anymore. The maize usually does better than wheat; I expect around 900 jin per mu if the weather is decent.

My total costs this year will be about 850 yuan. That's a lot for us — fertilizer prices keep climbing — but if I cut back too much and the weather turns against me, I'll regret it. My neighbor Old Zhang has 6 mu and his son helps with machinery, so he can afford to experiment. I watch what he does, but I don't copy everything — his soil is better and he has more cash. At our age, with only 3.8 mu, steady is better than sorry. I need enough grain for the two of us and a little to sell for cash. I don't expect miracles — I just need to get through the year without a bad surprise.
